**Jian+ 2016 (Ulysses, about 1.4 AU or more, so not 1 AU).**
- Median speed is within ±25% at low latitudes and ±20% at 30–60° latitude.
- Median B is under-predicted by 20–84% at 30–60° latitude, except for MWO/NSO-WSA v2.2-Enlil v2.8.
- Enlil v2.8 strengthened B through an increased scaling factor. The alternative setting raises that factor from 2 to 4 and lowers the inner-boundary density from 200 to 125 cm⁻³.
- WSA v2.2-Enlil v2.8 matches density best. Other models over-predict density by up to ×2 (IPS tomography by ×3.4 at mid-latitudes).

**Reiss+ 2023 (Advances in Space Research, not Space Weather).** This ISWAT paper contains no new model scores. It recommends ME, MAE, RMSE, Pearson r, skill score against climatology, and event-based POD/FAR/TS. It also restates the HUXt-vs-MAS "within 6%" result.

- **Riley, Linker & Mikić 2013 (ensembles) and Riley+ 2015 (expansion factor):** no statistics extracted. The 2015 draft I found covers a few CRs and is mostly qualitative.

- **MacNeice 2009 RMSE of 99.8:** secondary only (quoted by Reiss 2016).
- **Owens+ 2013 (27-day persistence):** it reports skill scores only; I extracted no RMSE.

## Synthesis
Ambient-wind models at 1 AU, whether empirical (WSA, ESWF), hybrid (WSA-ENLIL, WSA/HUX, EUHFORIA) or full MHD (MAS/CORHEL), reach a speed RMSE of about 75–125 km/s, typically about 100. Their hourly correlations are only r ≈ 0.3–0.6. That is no better than 27-day persistence (RMSE ≈80–120, r ≈0.2–0.5), and MSE skill against climatology or persistence is near zero or negative (−0.34 to +0.05 for raw WSA). Density is the worst-reproduced plasma parameter, with r ≲ 0.3 (0.13 in Owens 2008; 0.09–0.27 in Jian 2015). Its bias depends on the configuration: WSA-ENLIL is roughly unbiased in mean or median (×1.0–1.3) but flattens the SIR compression peaks (maximum ≈×0.5, minimum ≈×2), while MAS-ENLIL, CORHEL and EUHFORIA 1.0.4 over-predict density, by up to ×2. B is under-predicted almost everywhere unless it is rescaled: about ×2 in Gressl 2014, a factor of 5 in median for the GONG-WSA-Enlil runs Jian 2015 tested (which leave out the operational scaling), and about 35–45% per component in Owens 2008. This traces back to the open-flux deficit, where observation-based open flux falls short by about ×2 or more (Linker 2017), which is why operational ENLIL applies a B scaling factor. In event-based terms, high-speed enhancements are detected with POD 0.37–0.64, FAR 0.25–0.5 and TS 0.28–0.5. Models tend to under-count streams (BS 0.5–0.9), and timing errors are about 1 day: mean |Δt| 0.5–2.1 d, with WSA-ENLIL arriving about 2 d early at solar minimum and EUHFORIA arriving late because it under-predicts speed. Assimilating data or adapting the model gives the largest verified gains: speed RMSE drops 18% (Lang & Owens 2019) and 31% (Lang 2021, roughly 114 → 79 km/s). For comparison, adaptive coefficients give 10–15% (Reiss 2020), gradient boosting about 21% (Bailey 2021), and an ensemble median about 9% (Reiss 2019, a single CR)."
